title: Purpose of the progress practice
blurb: State the three-part purpose of the progress practice and tell it apart from the purposes of the issues, risk and quality practices.
question: Which is a purpose of the progress practice: recording lessons, controlling changes to the baseline, or providing a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability?

teach.h: What the progress practice is for
teach.body: Formally, the progress practice has three aims: to establish mechanisms to monitor and compare actual achievements against those planned; to provide a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability; and to control any deviations that cause an exception. In plain English: know where you are, predict where you are heading, and act when the prediction falls outside the agreed limits.

teach.caption: Past (what happened), future (what will happen), action (what to do about it).
The progress practice rests on an overarching plan-do-check-act cycle.

items: Defining management levels and tolerances for progress control.
Applying two types of control: event-driven and time-driven.
Escalating when a breach of tolerance is forecast.
Using data and systems to track, forecast and present progress.

teach.h: Three key words: forecast, tolerance, exception
teach.body: A forecast is a prediction of future performance, made by extrapolating trends, using data or applying judgement. A tolerance is the permissible deviation above and below a plan's target before the next level must be told. An exception is a situation where it can be forecast that a deviation will go beyond the agreed tolerance. Note the word forecast: an exception does not need the breach to have happened.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a depot electrification project
teach.body: At Fenwick Bus Services, project manager Aisha Morgan is in stage 2 of fitting chargers at three depots. Each fortnight she compares installed chargers with the stage plan (monitor and compare), projects that the last depot will finish nine days late (forecast), and checks the stage time tolerance of plus or minus three weeks. As the forecast sits inside tolerance, she rearranges the work package schedule herself (control). No escalation is needed.

teach.h: What the forecast tells the project manager

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Capturing lessons happens within progress management, but it is not one of the three stated purposes. (2) Controlling changes to the baseline is the purpose of the issues practice, not progress. (3) Progress is not only backward-looking: providing a forecast for objectives and continued viability is part of its purpose.

items: Purpose 1: monitor and compare actual achievements against those planned.
Purpose 2: provide a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability.
Purpose 3: control any deviations that cause an exception.
An exception is a FORECAST deviation beyond agreed tolerance.

summary: You can now state the three-part purpose of the progress practice (monitor and compare, forecast, control deviations causing an exception) and link it to plan-do-check-act. You can also separate it from the purposes of the issues, quality and risk practices.

A.q: Which is a purpose of the progress practice?
options: To collect and assess issues and control baseline changes
To forecast the project's objectives and continued viability
To document user requirements and how they will be met
To identify, assess and control uncertainty in the project
A.why: The progress practice provides a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability, alongside monitoring and controlling deviations (manual 11.1).

whyNot.0: Collecting and assessing issues and controlling baseline changes is the purpose of the issues practice.
whyNot.2: Documenting user requirements and how they will be met is the purpose of the quality practice.
whyNot.3: Identifying, assessing and controlling uncertainty is the purpose of the risk practice.

A.q: Which cycle is the progress practice based on?
options: Develop, check, maintain, confirm
Capture, assess, recommend, decide
Identify, assess, plan, implement
Plan, do, check, act
A.why: Progress management rests on an overarching plan-do-check-act cycle.

whyNot.0: Develop, check, maintain and confirm are the business case technique steps.
whyNot.1: Capture, assess, recommend and decide are steps of the issues technique.
whyNot.2: Identify, assess, plan and implement are steps of the risk technique.

A.q: What does the progress practice compare actual achievements against?
options: The achievements that were planned
The benefits in the business case
The lessons from earlier projects
The risk appetite of the business
A.why: Its first purpose is to establish mechanisms to monitor and compare actual achievements against those planned.

whyNot.1: Benefits are reviewed through the business case practice; progress compares actuals with plans.
whyNot.2: Earlier lessons inform planning but are not the yardstick for progress.
whyNot.3: Risk appetite shapes risk tolerances; it is not what actual progress is compared with.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The progress practice aims to control any deviations that cause an [?].
options: issue
off-specification
exception
escalation
B.why: The third part of the purpose is to control any deviations causing an exception (manual 11.1).

whyNot.0: Issues are handled by the issues practice; the progress purpose refers to exceptions.
whyNot.1: An off-specification is a type of issue about a product not meeting its specification.
whyNot.3: Escalation is the action taken when an exception is forecast, not the term in the purpose.

B.q:
Which two statements about the purpose of the progress practice are correct?
1. It monitors and compares actual achievements against those planned.
2. It controls changes to the approved project baseline.
3. It provides a forecast for the project's continued viability.
4. It documents the user's quality requirements.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Monitoring and comparing actuals with plans (1) and forecasting objectives and continued viability (3) are both purposes of the progress practice.

whyNot.1: Statement 2 describes the issues practice (change control).
whyNot.2: Both statements describe other practices: issues (2) and quality (4).

B.q: Why does the progress practice look forward as well as back?
options: To record each lesson as it arises
To set the stage tolerances for the board
To approve requests for change sooner
To spot likely deviations before they occur
B.why: Forecasting lets the project manager see a likely deviation early and act, or escalate an exception, before the breach happens.

whyNot.0: Recording lessons is part of reviewing progress, but it is not why the practice forecasts.
whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are set by the project board, not produced by forecasting.
whyNot.2: Approving requests for change belongs to the issues practice and change control.

C.q: A stage is forecast to finish within its tolerances, but later than its target date. Which part of the progress purpose applies, and who acts?
options: Escalating an exception; the project board
Controlling a deviation; the project manager
Controlling a change; the change authority
Forecasting viability; the business layer
C.why: A deviation inside stage tolerance is controlled by the project manager, who can take corrective action in controlling a stage without escalation.

whyNot.0: No exception exists because the forecast is within stage tolerance.
whyNot.2: The change authority deals with requests for change, not a schedule deviation within tolerance.
whyNot.3: The business layer is involved when project tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.

C.q: Which term describes a prediction of future performance, and what is it based on?
options: A tolerance, based on the business layer's targets
A baseline, based on the approved management products
A forecast, based on trends, data and judgement
An exception, based on actual overspends to date
C.why: A forecast predicts future performance by extrapolating trends, using data or applying judgement.

whyNot.0: A tolerance is a permissible deviation from a target, not a prediction.
whyNot.1: A baseline is the approved set of products under change control, not a prediction.
whyNot.3: An exception rests on a forecast breach, not only on overspends already incurred.

C.q: A board member says the progress practice exists mainly to capture lessons. Which statement corrects this?
options: Its purposes are monitoring, forecasting and controlling deviations
Its purposes are capturing, assessing and controlling issues
Its purposes are setting tolerances and approving stage plans
Its purposes are planning products and estimating their costs
C.why: Lessons are reviewed and reported within progress management, but the stated purposes are to monitor and compare, forecast, and control deviations causing an exception.

whyNot.1: Capturing and assessing issues and controlling change is the issues practice.
whyNot.2: Setting stage tolerances and approving stage plans are board responsibilities, not the practice's purpose.
whyNot.3: Planning products and estimating costs belongs to the plans practice.

reteach.title: A satnav for the project
reteach.question: How is the progress practice like a satnav on a long drive?

blocks.h: Where am I, when will I arrive, do I need to reroute?
blocks.body: A satnav compares where you are with the route (monitor and compare), predicts your arrival time (forecast) and reroutes when a jam would make you too late (control the deviation). If the new arrival time is outside what your host accepted, you phone ahead before you are late. That is the progress practice in miniature: monitor, forecast, control, and escalate an exception early.

blocks.text: Keeping a trip diary is useful, but it is not why the satnav exists. In the same way, lessons sit inside progress management but are not one of its three purposes.

explain.body: The first aim is to set up mechanisms that monitor actual achievements and compare them with what was planned.

test.q: Which is a purpose of the progress practice?
options: To agree the project's management approaches
To appoint the project management team
To prioritize the user's acceptance criteria
To compare actual achievements with the plan
test.why: Monitoring and comparing actual achievements against those planned is the first part of the purpose.

whyNot.0: Management approaches are agreed in initiating a project; this is not the practice's purpose.
whyNot.1: Appointing the team belongs to starting up a project and the organizing practice.
whyNot.2: Prioritizing acceptance criteria belongs to the quality practice.

explain.body: The second aim is a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability: where the plan is heading, not only where it has been.

test.q: The progress practice provides a forecast for which two things?
options: Stage risks and open stage issues
Objectives and continued viability
Benefits and user acceptance
Products and quality criteria
test.why: It provides a forecast for the project's objectives and continued viability (manual 11.1).

whyNot.0: Risks and issues are recorded in their registers; the purpose names objectives and viability.
whyNot.2: Benefits are part of viability, but user acceptance is not what the purpose forecasts.
whyNot.3: Products and quality criteria belong to the plans and quality practices.

explain.body: The third aim is to control any deviations that cause an exception, so the right level decides what happens next.

test.q: Which deviations does the progress practice aim to control?
options: Deviations that cause an exception
Deviations recorded in the daily log
Deviations that change the benefits
Deviations raised by the senior user
test.why: The purpose refers to controlling any deviations that cause an exception.

whyNot.1: The daily log is a record, not the test of which deviations are controlled.
whyNot.2: A change in benefits forecasts can sit within tolerance and need no exception; the purpose names deviations that cause an exception.
whyNot.3: Who raises a deviation does not define the purpose.

explain.body: Progress management is based on an overarching plan-do-check-act cycle: set targets, do the work, check actuals and forecasts, then act.

test.q: In the plan-do-check-act cycle behind the progress practice, which step compares actuals and forecasts with the plan?
options: Plan
Do
Check
Act
test.why: The check step compares actual achievement and forecasts against the plan before action is taken.

whyNot.0: Plan sets the targets and tolerances.
whyNot.1: Do is the delivery of the work itself.
whyNot.3: Act responds to what the check found, through corrective action or escalation.
